marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q029.takeaway: The middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior interventricular groove, not the posterior atrioventricular groove; that statement is wrong.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q029.displayText:
The middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior interventricular groove, not the posterior atrioventricular groove; that statement is wrong.

The wrong statement is that the middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior atrioventricular groove; the source places it in the posterior interventricular groove. The opening of the coronary sinus may be guarded by the semilunar Thebesian valve. The great cardiac vein accompanies the anterior interventricular/LAD artery in the anterior interventricular groove, and venae cordis minimae (Thebesian veins) open into all cardiac chambers.
emphasis: The middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior interventricular groove, not the posterior atrioventricular groove; that statement is wrong

rationales.a: The Thebesian valve guards the coronary sinus opening into right atrium.
rationales.c: Great cardiac vein accompanies LAD in anterior interventricular groove.
rationales.d: Venae cordis minimae can drain into any of the four chambers.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q030.takeaway: Anterior cardiac veins drain directly to the right atrium and are least affected by coronary-sinus obstruction.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q030.displayText:
Anterior cardiac veins drain directly to the right atrium and are least affected by coronary-sinus obstruction.

The anterior cardiac veins are least likely to dilate because they drain directly into the right atrium rather than through the coronary sinus.
emphasis: Anterior cardiac veins drain directly to the right atrium and are least affected by coronary-sinus obstruction

rationales.a: Middle cardiac vein drains to coronary sinus and can dilate upstream of obstruction.
rationales.b: Small cardiac vein drains into coronary sinus.
rationales.c: Oblique vein of left atrium drains into coronary sinus.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q031.takeaway: The small cardiac vein drains to the coronary sinus and does not open directly into the sinus venarum of the right atrium.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q031.displayText:
The small cardiac vein drains to the coronary sinus and does not open directly into the sinus venarum of the right atrium.

The small cardiac vein does not open directly into the sinus venarum; it opens into the coronary sinus. The superior vena cava, coronary sinus and inferior vena cava open into the sinus venarum, the smooth posterior part of the right atrium.
emphasis: The small cardiac vein drains to the coronary sinus and does not open directly into the sinus venarum of the right atrium

rationales.a: SVC opens into the sinus venarum.
rationales.b: The coronary sinus opens into the right atrium near the IVC orifice.
rationales.c: IVC opens into the sinus venarum.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q032.takeaway: Cardiac sympathetic outflow arises from upper thoracic spinal segments T1–T5.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q032.displayText:
Cardiac sympathetic outflow arises from upper thoracic spinal segments T1–T5.

Sympathetic innervation of the heart is from T1-T5. Preganglionic sympathetic fibers arise from T1-T5; some synapse in upper thoracic sympathetic ganglia and others in cervical ganglia. Postganglionic fibers from these ganglia form the sympathetic cardiac nerves and innervate the heart.
emphasis: Cardiac sympathetic outflow arises from upper thoracic spinal segments T1–T5

rationales.a: T1–T3 omits the lower thoracic contribution through T5.
rationales.c: T3–T7 extends below and omits upper segments.
rationales.d: L1–L5 are lumbar levels and do not provide cardiac sympathetic outflow.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q033.takeaway: The ganglion of Wrisberg lies below and slightly anterior to the aortic arch, near the right side of the ligamentum arteriosum.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q033.displayText:
The ganglion of Wrisberg lies below and slightly anterior to the aortic arch, near the right side of the ligamentum arteriosum.

The cardiac ganglion of Wrisberg is present in the superficial cardiac plexus immediately below and slightly in front of the arch of the aorta, to the right of the ligamentum arteriosum.
emphasis: The ganglion of Wrisberg lies below and slightly anterior to the aortic arch, near the right side of the ligamentum arteriosum

rationales.b: It lies beneath rather than above the arch.
rationales.c: It is right of, not left of, the ligamentum arteriosum.
rationales.d: It lies anterior to the ligament rather than posterior to it.
